REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - OCTOBER 14, 2021 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
* COVID-19 NOTICE *
To protect public health and safety during the COVID-19 pandemic and in compliance with the current State Department of Public Health and Los Angeles County Health Officer Orders and City of Cerritos COVID-19 Safety Plan, the City Council Chamber will be open to the public. As authorized by State of California Executive Orders N-25-20, N-29-20, and N-08-21, and subsequently by Assembly Bill 361 (Chapter 165, Statutes of 2021), this meeting may also be conducted via teleconference, if necessary. Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in-person in the Council Chamber subject to posted COVID-19 protocols.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in-person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

During this part of the meeting the City Manager/Executive Director or designated staff will have an opportunity to report on various City matters and/or respond verbally to questions or comments from the prior City Council meeting, including any request by the City Council to provide a brief supplemental report or brief follow-up response to items from the prior City Council meeting’s agenda.
11B.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, requests may be made of the staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item.

After the City Council/Successor Agency reconvenes into Open Session, designated City staff will provide a verbal report on any reportable action taken in Closed Session. This report will be memorialized in the official meeting minutes.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY,
OCTOBER 14, 2021, 7:00 P.M., IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL,
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Dustin T. Parker, Concordia Lutheran Church.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Girl Scout Troop 963.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Bruce Barrows
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Chuong Vo
  Mayor/Chair Grace Hu

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to excuse Council/Agency
  Member Naresh Solanki from the Thursday, October 14, 2021, 7:00 p.m., City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Solanki (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  A Proclamation was issued by the City Council as follows:

  Friends of the Cerritos Library (National Friends of Libraries Week).

  The City Clerk administered the oath of office to incoming Fine Arts and Historical
  Commissioner Judy Chiu.

5B.  Informational update on the City's response to the COVID-19 pandemic and other City
  events, services, and programs.

  An informational report was given by Annie Hylton, City Librarian & Marketing Manager.
  A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  There was no further action taken on this item.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to approve the Monday,
  September 27, 2021, 7:00 p.m., City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes

  City of Cerritos  October 14, 2021  $12,698,189.85 (COUNCIL)

  City Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending August 31, 2021

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending August 31, 2021

  The motion carried (4 – 0 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Solanki (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, October 14, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 3 of 8

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7D.  Award of contract for the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts Mailing List Acquisition
  Services, RFP No. 1435-21 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to:

  1. Award a contract for the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts Mailing List Acquisition
  Services to Carney Direct Marketing, in the amount of $21,600 with the following
  provisions:

  a. The term of the contract shall begin upon the City Council's award of bid and
  extends for 18 months. The term of the agreement may be extended by mutual
  agreement of both parties for up to three additional 12-month terms. Upon the
  completion of the 18-month period of the agreement, the list acquisition services
  firm may request that the City approve an increase in the project fees for work to
  be completed for the additional period. Such requests for increase shall be based
  on the Consumer Price Index of the Bureau of Labor Statistics, U.S. Department
  of Labor, Los Angeles – Long Beach metropolitan area for the period of July 1
  through June 30 of the calendar year immediately preceding the date of such
  adjustment. The maximum increase for any period shall be 3 percent (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Solanki (excused)

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration of a request by Cerritos Community College District to renew
  an existing temporary use permit for the continued operation of a temporary automobile
  storage facility on a portion of the Cerritos College campus. The subject property is
  located on the northeast corner of 166th Street and Studebaker Road at 11001 166th
  Street, Cerritos, California, 90703 and is zoned open space (OS) (APNS 7016-007-906
  and 7016-007-909) (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments period.

  Phillip Satterfield expressed concern with extending the temporary use permit citing
  negative impacts to his adjacent residential neighborhood.

  Mel Cortez spoke in support of the extension of the temporary use permit.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the Mayor
  declared the public comments period and public hearing closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Hu, to:

  1. Waive full reading of and adopt the resolution captioned below, authorizing the City
  of Cerritos to issue Temporary Use Permit 2021-19 to the Cerritos Community
  College District, for the Cerritos Community College District’s continued operation of
  a temporary automobile storage facility on a portion of the Cerritos College campus
  for a five (5) year period:

  Resolution No. 2021-22, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
  COMMUNITY COLLEGE DISTRICT TO RENEW AN EXISTING TEMPORARY
  USE PERMIT FOR THE CONTINUED OPERATION OF A TEMPORARY
  AUTOMOBILE STORAGE FACILITY ON A PORTION OF THE CERRITOS
  COLLEGE CAMPUS. THE SUBJECT PROPERTY IS LOCATED ON THE
  NORTHEAST CORNER OF 166TH STREET AND STUDEBAKER ROAD AT
  11001 166TH STREET, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA, 90703 AND IS ZONED
  OPEN SPACE (OS) (APNS 7016-007-906 AND 7016-007-909) (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Solanki (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

(minutes continue on the next page)
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, October 14, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 5 of 8

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of legal and administrative matters related to the 2022
  Cerritos General Municipal Election (COUNCIL).

  Waiver of full reading of and introduction of AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS,
  CALIFORNIA, ESTABLISHING THE CITY’S GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION DATE AS THE
  SECOND TURESDAY OF APRIL IN EACH EVEN-NUMBERED YEAR AND ADDING SECTION
  2.40.030 TO THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE PROVIDING FOR THE PROCEDURE FOR
  HOLDING ELECTIONS AS AUTHORIZED BY THE CERRITOS CITY CHARTER AND THE
  CALIFORNIA ELECTIONS CODE, AND REPEALING ORDINANCE 1019 (COUNCIL).

  Staff reports were given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer, and Bill Ihrke, City
  Attorney. A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no other individuals
  who elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period
  closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to:

  1. Waive full reading of and introduce Ordinance No. 1036, AN ORDINANCE OF THE
  CITY OF CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA, ESTABLISHING THE CITY’S GENERAL
  MUNICIPAL ELECTION DATE AS THE SECOND TUESDAY OF APRIL IN EACH
  EVEN-NUMBERED YEAR AND ADDING SECTION 2.40.030 TO THE CERRITOS
  MUNICIPAL CODE PROVIDING FOR THE PROCEDURE FOR HOLDING
  ELECTIONS AS AUTHORIZED BY THE CERRITOS CITY CHARTER AND THE
  CALIFORNIA ELECTIONS CODE, AND REPEALING ORDINANCE 1019; and

  2. Authorize a new allocation in the Fiscal Year 2021-22 Comprehensive Annual
  Financial Program (City Budget) in the amount of $100,000 from the City’s General
  Fund for the purpose of conducting the 2022 City of Cerritos General Municipal
  Election as a stand-alone proceeding, inclusive of the potential one-time purchase of
  equipment which will off-set future election-related costs to the City and the
  potential placement of one or more proposed Charter amendment measures on the
  ballot. If the equipment is not purchased and/or the 2021 Charter Review process
  does not result in the placement of any measures on the 2022 ballot, the amount
  allocated for such purposes will then be returned to the General Fund; and

  3. Authorize the City of Cerritos, by way of the City Manager or designee, to enter into
  the necessary agreements with the City of Whittier, State-certified vendors, and
  elections consultants for the necessary elections equipment, materials, supplies, and
  services; and

  4. Authorize the City Clerk and authorized designee(s) to oversee and conduct the City
  of Cerritos Municipal Election in accordance with the Cerritos Charter and applicable
  laws and regulations (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (3 – 1 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  Yokoyama
  ABSENT:  Solanki (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, October 14, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 6 of 8

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who

9C.  Review and consideration of award of a contract for the annual mechanical equipment
  maintenance services, Bid No. 1440-21 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kanna Vancheswaran, Director of Public Works/Water &
  Power. A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no other individuals
  who elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period
  closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Barrows, to:

  1.  Reject all bids and authorize staff to re-advertise the project; and

  2.  Authorize staff to extend the current contract with South Coast Mechanical, Inc.
  with the existing terms and rates on a month-to-month basis (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Solanki (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

(minutes continue on the next page)
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, October 14, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 7 of 8

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9D.  Review and consideration of award of a contract for generator and related hardware
  services, RFP No. 1441-21 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kanna Vancheswaran, Director of Public Works/Water &
  Power. A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period
  closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Hu, to:

  1. Award a contract for generator and related hardware services, RFP No. 1441-21 to
  Global Power Group, Inc., in the amount of $140,258.00, with the following
  provisions:

  a. The term of the contract is for one (1) year, starting from the date of issuance of
  the Notice to Proceed; and
  b. The contract provides for up to three (3) one-year extensions, providing both
  parties with to continue the agreement under the existing terms; and

  2. Reject the other proposal; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any contract-related change
  orders (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Solanki (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

11B.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports
